glue.does: Buys you a second while you think: "um, let me see."

examples.ja: «えっと»…{二|ふた}つお{願|ねが}いします。
«えっと»、{駅|えき}はどこですか。
examples.en: Let me see, where's the station?

glue.listen: Everywhere: people answering questions, ordering, giving directions.
glue.note: Your best friend as a learner. It holds your turn so the other person waits.

glue.does: Gets someone's attention politely, or hesitates before asking: "um, excuse me…"

examples.ja: «あの»、すみません。
«あの»…ちょっと{聞|き}いてもいいですか。
examples.en: Um… can I ask you something?

glue.listen: Before almost every question to a stranger.
glue.note: Softer than すみません alone. Drawn out (あのー) it sounds hesitant.

glue.does: "Well…": softens an answer, makes it less absolute.

examples.ja: «まあ»、{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}です。
«まあ»、{少|すこ}しだけ{分|わ}かります。

glue.listen: When someone doesn't want to sound too strong or is shrugging something off.

glue.does: "Like…" / "kind of": a casual filler, or "something".

examples.ja: «なんか»{寒|さむ}くない？
«なんか»{食|た}べたいな。
examples.en: I kind of want to eat something.

glue.listen: Constantly in casual talk, anime and dramas. Friends, not strangers.

glue.does: Thinking sound: "hmm." Also a gentle way to start a no.

examples.ja: «うーん»、どうしよう。
«うーん»、ちょっと{難|むずか}しいですね。

glue.listen: When people are deciding, or about to politely say no.
glue.note: 「うーん、ちょっと…」 is very often a no.

glue.does: "A bit", and the softest way to say no: trail off with ちょっと….

examples.ja: «ちょっと»{待|ま}ってください。
{明日|あした}は«ちょっと»…
examples.en: Tomorrow is a bit… (= I can't.)

glue.listen: Constantly. Listen for it trailing off: that's a polite refusal.

glue.does: "Oh, really? / Is that so?" Shows you're following and interested.

examples.ja: A：{去年|きょねん}、{九州|きゅうしゅう}に{住|す}んでいました。 B：«そうなんですか»。
examples.en: A: I lived in Kyushu last year. B: Oh, really?

glue.listen: Every conversation with someone you've just met.

glue.does: Casual "oh, I see / huh, really."

examples.ja: A：{明日|あした}、{休|やす}みなんだ。 B：«そうなんだ»！
examples.en: A: I'm off tomorrow. B: Oh, nice!

glue.listen: Friends talking. Dramas and Midnight Diner regulars.

glue.does: "Huh! / Wow": mild surprise or interest.

examples.ja: «へえ»、すごいですね。
«へえ»、{知|し}らなかった。

glue.listen: Any time someone hears something new. Rising tone = interested.

glue.does: "I see / that makes sense": you understood the explanation.

examples.ja: «なるほど»、{分|わ}かりました。
«なるほど»ね。

glue.listen: When someone explains something. Avoid it with your boss or elders; use そうなんですね there.

glue.does: "True / good point": agreeing with what was said.

examples.ja: «たしかに»{高|たか}いですね。
A：{電車|でんしゃ}のほうが{早|はや}いよ。 B：«たしかに»。
examples.en: A: The train's faster. B: Good point.

glue.listen: Conversations where someone makes a point. Very common among friends.

glue.does: "That's right" or, said slowly, "let me think…".

examples.ja: A：{寒|さむ}いですね。 B：«そうですね»。
examples.en: A: Cold, isn't it? B: It is.

examples.ja: «そうですね»…{日曜日|にちようび}はどうですか。
examples.en: Let me see… how about Sunday?

glue.listen: Small talk with strangers, interviews, shopkeepers. Two jobs: agreeing, and stalling.

glue.does: "Really?" Surprise or checking.

examples.ja: «{本当|ほんとう}»？よかった！
«{本当|ほんとう}»ですか。

glue.listen: Any surprise. ほんと？ is the quicker casual form.

glue.does: "But / though": casual. Starts a sentence or joins two.

examples.ja: {行|い}きたいんだ«けど»、{時間|じかん}がない。
examples.en: I want to go, but I don't have time.

examples.ja: «だけど»、{雨|あめ}だよ。

glue.listen: Casual talk everywhere. Polite version: ですが or でも.
glue.note: At the end of a sentence it trails off to soften: 「ちょっと{聞|き}きたいんだけど…」

glue.does: "But": starts a sentence that pushes back on the last one.

examples.ja: おいしいです。«でも»、ちょっと{高|たか}いです。
examples.en: It's delicious. But a bit expensive.

examples.ja: «でも»、{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}です。

glue.listen: The most common "but" at the start of a sentence, polite or casual.

glue.does: "So / that's why": what follows comes from what came before.

examples.ja: {雨|あめ}だった。«だから»、{家|いえ}にいた。
examples.en: It was raining. So I stayed home.

examples.ja: «だから»、{言|い}ったでしょう。
examples.en: See, that's what I told you.

glue.listen: Explanations, and mild told-you-so. Polite: ですから.

glue.does: "And then / so": moves a story forward, or asks "and?"

examples.ja: «それで»、どうしましたか。
examples.en: And then what did you do?

examples.ja: {電車|でんしゃ}が{止|と}まって、«それで»{遅|おく}れました。
examples.en: The train stopped, and so I was late.

glue.listen: Storytelling, and listeners prompting the next part.

glue.does: "Well then / in that case": moves to a decision or the next step.

examples.ja: «じゃあ»、これをください。
«じゃあ»、また{明日|あした}。

glue.listen: Ordering, ending conversations, making plans. Polite: では.

glue.does: "Besides / on top of that": adds another reason.

examples.ja: {安|やす}いし、«それに»おいしい。
examples.en: It's cheap, and on top of that, it's good.

glue.listen: When someone is listing reasons or selling something.

glue.does: "By the way": changes the subject.

examples.ja: «ところで»、{明日|あした}は{何|なに}をしますか。
examples.en: By the way, what are you doing tomorrow?

glue.listen: Small talk turning a corner.

glue.does: "For now / to start with." Also the famous first-order phrase.

examples.ja: «とりあえず»{生|なま}ビール！
«とりあえず»、{駅|えき}に{行|い}きましょう。
examples.en: For now, let's head to the station.

glue.listen: Izakaya, every single night. And planning.

glue.does: "Actually… / to tell the truth": introduces news or a confession.

examples.ja: «{実|じつ}は»、{作曲家|さっきょくか}なんです。
«{実|じつ}は»、ちょっとお{願|ねが}いがあるんですが…
examples.en: Actually, I have a small favor to ask…

glue.listen: Before anything surprising or personal.

glue.does: "Just as I thought / after all": something confirmed, or a change of mind.

examples.ja: «やっぱり»{日本|にほん}のコーヒーはおいしい。
examples.en: Japanese coffee really is good, just as I thought.

examples.ja: «やっぱり»、{行|い}きます。

glue.listen: Constantly. Casual: やっぱ.

glue.does: Trailing "…but": leaves a request or fact hanging so it sounds soft.

examples.ja: すみません、{予約|よやく}したクラインです«けど»…
examples.en: Excuse me, I'm Kline, I have a reservation…

examples.ja: ちょっと{聞|き}きたいんです«けど»…

glue.listen: Requests at counters and on the phone. The listener finishes the thought for you.

glue.does: "I wonder…": thinking aloud, softer than a question.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}は{雨|あめ}«かな»。
examples.en: I wonder if it'll rain tomorrow.

examples.ja: これでいい«かな»？

glue.listen: Self-talk and gentle questions. Polite: 〜でしょうか.

glue.does: "…right?": checks the other person agrees with something you both know.

examples.ja: これ、おいしい«よね»。
{明日|あした}は{休|やす}みです«よね»？

glue.listen: Building agreement in conversation.

glue.does: "…was it?": you're trying to remember something.

examples.ja: {名前|なまえ}、{何|なん}だった«っけ»？
{何時|なんじ}だった«っけ»。

glue.listen: Whenever someone has forgotten something. Useful for you!

glue.does: "…right? / probably": assumes, or invites agreement.

examples.ja: {寒|さむ}い«でしょう»。
{明日|あした}は{晴|は}れる«でしょう»。

glue.listen: Weather forecasts (でしょう), and friends (でしょ↑).

glue.does: "Seems like / looks like".

examples.ja: {雨|あめ}«みたい»です。
{閉|し}まっている«みたい»。

glue.listen: Describing what you observe. Very natural.

glue.does: Casual quote: "they say / you mean…?" Also a casual topic marker.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}、{雨|あめ}だ«って»。
「おまかせ」«って»{何|なん}ですか。

glue.listen: Relaying what someone said, and asking what words mean.

glue.does: "…isn't it / huh": shares a feeling, invites agreement.

examples.ja: いい{天気|てんき}です«ね»。
おいしい«ね»！

glue.listen: Every small-talk sentence. Missing ね can sound cold.

glue.does: "…you know / I'm telling you": gives new information.

examples.ja: この{店|みせ}、おいしいです«よ»。
examples.en: This place is good, you know.

examples.ja: {電車|でんしゃ}、{来|き}ました«よ»。

glue.listen: Recommendations and alerts. Overused, it can sound pushy.

glue.does: "…and (also)": lists reasons, often with the main point left unsaid.

examples.ja: {安|やす}い«し»、{近|ちか}いし、ここにしよう。
examples.en: It's cheap, it's close… let's go here.

glue.listen: Giving reasons, often trailing off.

glue.does: "Amazing / wow": all-purpose praise or surprise.

examples.ja: «すごい»ですね！
«すごい»{人|ひと}！

glue.listen: Everywhere. Also means "really, very": すごくおいしい.

glue.does: "Just what I'd expect from you": praise that someone lived up to their reputation.

examples.ja: «さすが»ですね！
«さすが»{日本|にほん}！

glue.listen: When someone skilled does something well.

glue.does: "Oh good / I'm glad": relief.

examples.ja: «よかった»！{間|ま}に{合|あ}った。
{元気|げんき}そうで«よかった»です。

glue.listen: Any good news or relief.

glue.does: "OK / fine / no thanks": also a polite "I'm good."

examples.ja: «{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}»ですか。
{袋|ふくろ}は«{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}»です。
examples.en: I don't need a bag, thanks.

glue.listen: Shops ("bag?" → 大丈夫です = no thanks), and checking on someone.
glue.note: Careful: as an answer to an offer it usually means no.

glue.does: "Can't be helped / oh well."

examples.ja: {雨|あめ}だから、«しょうがない»。
まあ、«しょうがない»ね。

glue.listen: Shrugging off bad luck. Same as 仕方がない, which you know from WaniKani.

glue.does: "Thanks for your work / good job": after effort, at the end of a day or a rehearsal.

examples.ja: «お{疲|つか}れさま»でした！

glue.listen: End of every rehearsal, recording session and work day. You'll say it a lot.

glue.does: "Oh no!" or "insane (good)": slangy, depends on tone.

examples.ja: «やばい»、{遅|おく}れる！
examples.en: Oh no, I'm going to be late!

examples.ja: このラーメン、«やばい»！

glue.listen: Young people, anime, TV. Recognize it; use it with friends only.

glue.does: "Just in case / sort of / for the record": hedges.

examples.ja: «{一応|いちおう}»、{予約|よやく}しました。
examples.en: I made a reservation, just in case.

examples.ja: «{一応|いちおう}»、{作曲家|さっきょくか}です。

glue.listen: Very common hedge. Modest people use it about themselves.

glue.does: "Since you went to the trouble / since we're here": don't waste the chance.

examples.ja: «せっかく»{九州|きゅうしゅう}に{来|き}たから、ラーメンを{食|た}べたい。
examples.en: Since I came all the way to Kyushu, I want ramen.

examples.ja: «せっかく»だから、{写真|しゃしん}を{撮|と}りましょう。
examples.en: Since we're here, let's take a photo.

glue.listen: Travel talk, constantly. Very you.

glue.does: Casual "why?"

examples.ja: «なんで»？
«なんで»{日本|にほん}に{来|き}たの？
examples.en: Why did you come to Japan?

glue.listen: Friends asking you questions. Polite: どうして.
